newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Alan Bond sentenced to four years jail.
newsitem.headline: Australian Alan Bond sentenced to four years jail.

text.p: Failed Australian entrepreneur Alan Bond was on Wednesday sentenced to four years in prison for his role in the biggest corporate fraud in Australian history worth A$1.0 billion (US$766 million).
But Bond could be released on parole from prison in 1998 after serving a minimum one-year non-parole period.

Bond, 58, already serving a three-year sentence for an earlier fraud, pleaded guilty to two charges of dishonesty last December. Bond stood impassively in the Western Australia Supreme Court dock when the sentence was handed down.
Judge Michael Murray said the latest sentence was to be served concurrently with his present sentence, which would have seen him released in August 1997.
After serving the one-year minimum non-parole period of his latest sentence, Bond would be eligible for release in 1998.
The prosecutor had asked the judge to jail Bond for a maximum 10 years.

Bond admitted that in 1988 and 1989 he failed to act honestly as a company director and acted with intent to defraud when he created a A$1.0 billion unsecured loan from Bell Resources to his ailing Bond Corp.
Bond pleaded guilty after the prosecution agreed to drop a further five charges relating to the Bell Resources fraud which followed Bond Corp taking control of the Bell Group Ltd in mid-1988.
Bond was jailed for three years in August for fraud involving the French impressionist painting, La Promenade.

He was also jailed for two-and-a-half years in 1992 after being found guilty of inducing a former friend to contribute to the rescue of a Western Australia bank while concealing a A$16 million fee for his own company.
He served only a few months in jail before a second jury acquitted him at a re-trial.
Bond was named Australian of the Year after winning the America's Cup yacht race in 1983.

His personal fortune was estimated at A$350 million in the late 1980s before the collapse of his brewing, mining and property empire, Bond Corporation Holdings Ltd, under a pile of debt totalling A$600 million.

Bond, a former signwriter who built a global network of companies with interests spanning mining, property, media and breweries, was declared bankrupt in April 1995, but was freed of bankruptcy in February 1996.
